incumbent.name: Jim Lucas
incumbent.summary: Jim Lucas, a Seymour business owner and Marine Corps veteran, has represented House District 69 since 2012 {lucas_bio}. He was reelected in 2024 with 68.7% of the vote {wiki_2026}.
record: Committees: Financial Institutions, Veterans Affairs and Public Safety, and Public Policy, according to his caucus biography {lucas_bio}.

2023: Authored a law creating an optional, state-funded 40-hour firearms training course for school staff who are allowed to carry {lucas_teacher}. 2024: Authored HEA 1142, creating the Hoosier First Responder Medal of Honor {lucas_medal}. 2025: Co-authored HEA 1114, raising penalties for unlicensed drivers who cause injury or death {lucas_hea1114}.

Voted yes on SEA 1, the 2025 property-tax law (April 10, 2025) {rc_sea1_433}; the 2025 budget conference report, HEA 1001 (April 25, 2025) {rc_hb1001_576}; and HB 1032, the congressional redistricting bill (Dec. 5, 2025) {rc_hb1032_28}.

race_context: House District 69 includes portions of Bartholomew, Jackson, Scott and Washington counties, according to the House Republican caucus {lucas_bio}; The Indiana Citizen describes it as representing Seymour, Brownstown and Salem {citizen_rural}. (It does not include Jennings County, which is mostly in House District 67.)

Lucas and Chris Bowen were each the only declared candidate in their party's May 5, 2026 primary {wiki_2026}. Tyler J. Henkle is on the ballot as an independent, making this a three-candidate race {in_list}.
No debate or candidate forum for this race was found.

candidates.summary: Seven-term Republican incumbent from Seymour seeking reelection {lucas_bio} {wiki_2026}.
background: U.S. Marine Corps veteran and small-business owner (The Awning Guy, Inc.); formerly served on the Seymour City Council {lucas_bio}.
path_to_ballot: Unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary {wiki_2026}.

items: His caucus biography lists "protecting the right to bear arms" among his top priorities, along with jobs, fiscal integrity and education {lucas_bio}.
On school staff firearms training: "I want our schools to have every available option to boost security and be a deterrent to anyone looking to do harm" {lucas_teacher}.
Told students in 2024 that more gun laws would not stop people "who aren't being stopped by the hundreds of existing laws right now" {ibj_gun}.

candidates.summary: Democratic nominee from Seymour who filed in January 2026 as part of the Indiana Rural Summit coalition's candidate filing event {citizen_rural}.
path_to_ballot: Filed Jan. 7, 2026 with the Indiana Rural Summit, a nonprofit that trains Democratic candidates from rural and small-town Indiana {citizen_rural}; unopposed in the May 5 Democratic primary {wiki_2026}.

items: Said she was motivated to run by the legislature's passage of laws restricting abortion {citizen_rural}.
Cited laws she said limit access to the ballot box as a reason for running {citizen_rural}.

on_incumbent: Said Lucas does not listen to constituents' concerns and "just does what he wants" (as paraphrased by The Indiana Citizen); said, "Even if I don't agree, if that's what most of my constituents want, that's the way I'll vote" {citizen_rural}.
plans: "I just want to be the voice for the people" {citizen_rural}.

review_flags.summary: May 31, 2023: Crashed his pickup through a guardrail at I-65 and Indiana 11 and drove away; a trooper's affidavit reported a 0.097% portable breath test more than an hour later. On June 12, 2023 he pleaded guilty to misdemeanor operating while intoxicated and leaving the scene, receiving suspended sentences, probation and about $4,000 in restitution; he kept his seat. He said he took "full responsibility," apologized and was "already enrolled in counseling" {ibj_plea}. In December 2023 a judge ended his probation after six months, finding he had completed its conditions {ibj_probation}.
review_flags.note: Misdemeanor OWI and leaving-the-scene plea, 2023; probation ended early. Previously shown in the public profile.

review_flags.summary: Jan. 30, 2024: Briefly opened his jacket to show a holstered handgun while talking with Muncie students at a gun-safety rally. Speaker Todd Huston said he should not have done so; Democratic leaders criticized it {wfyi_gun}. Lucas said "There was no intimidation whatsoever" and that the episode was "being intentionally blown out of proportion" {ibj_gun}.
review_flags.note: Showing a holstered handgun to students at a gun-safety rally; relates to his gun-policy work. Previously shown in the public profile.

review_flags.summary: August 2022: Was criticized, including by the CANDLES Holocaust Museum, for a Facebook cover photo with a quote attributed to Joseph Goebbels; he deleted it and replaced it with a different quote. The report noted earlier criticism of his social-media posts and that Speaker Huston had previously removed him from study committees over a meme {ipm_goebbels}.
review_flags.note: Removed from the profile as non-policy. Other 2017-2022 social-media controversies were not read in full.
